analysis.title: Pfizer Inc. (PFE): 3Q26 First Take — Beat and Modest Raise vs Muted Expectations
key_insights: PFE reported 3Q26 revenue of $16.6bn against GS consensus of $16.0bn and Visible Alpha consensus of $15.9bn. Adjusted EPS including guided IPR&D was $0.87 against $0.74 (GS) and $0.73 (consensus).

Key products across primary care, specialty care and oncology were generally stronger than GS and Visible Alpha consensus expected. Paxlovid ($449mn), Nurtec ($547mn), Xeljanz ($213mn), Adcetris ($231mn) and Ibrance ($1,082mn) beat both GS and consensus.

Prevnar Family missed consensus ($1,564mn vs $1,607mn). The company cited lower US adult and pediatric vaccination rates, market share erosion in the adult indication, and lower pediatric demand in certain international markets. GS expects this to be a focus of the call.
Eliquis revenue of $2,523mn beat consensus ($2,383mn) on pricing tailwinds and was in line with GS ($2,539mn).

FY2026 revenue guidance was raised by $1.5bn at the midpoint to $62.0bn-$64.0bn. Adjusted diluted EPS guidance was raised and narrowed from $2.80-$3.00 to $2.95-$3.05, including an unfavorable IPR&D impact of $0.10. The company points to product mix, productivity and cost management supporting margin expansion.
Management reiterated line of sight to a risk-adjusted high-single digit revenue CAGR from year-end 2028 through year-end 2033. GS notes this is not reflected in Street forecasts.
The mevrometostat MEVPRO-1 trial readout moved from 4Q26 to 1Q27 based on the current event rate. GS sees no material clinical catalysts left this year.
Cecile Guegan was confirmed as permanent CFO after serving as interim CFO.
Gross margin was 76.8% against 74.7% (GS) and 75.5% (consensus). Adjusted EBIT ex. IPR&D was $6,577mn, 9.3% above GS and 10.6% above consensus.
GS maintains a Neutral rating with a $26 12-month price target (9.0x Q5-Q8 adjusted EPS), 15.2% below the $30.67 close on 2 Nov 2026.

Call topics GS will watch: guidance puts and takes and the preliminary 2027 outlook expected in December, the new CFO's capital allocation priorities (BD, dividend commitment), the impact of additional cost-cutting on the pipeline, and framing of upcoming GLP-1/amylin Ph1/2 data against competitor updates.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Neutral and a $26 target, 15.2% below the $30.67 price, after a 3Q26 beat and guidance raise. The target uses 9.0x Q5-Q8 adjusted EPS.

earnings_insights: PFE 3Q26 reported 11/3: revenue $16,583mn vs GS est $15,997mn and Visible Alpha consensus $15,850mn (note text cites consensus as $15.9bn).
PFE 3Q26 reported 11/3: adjusted EPS including guided IPR&D $0.87 vs GS est $0.74 and consensus $0.73.
PFE 3Q26 reported 11/3: gross margin 76.8% vs GS est 74.7% and consensus 75.5%. R&D was 17.7% of revenue and SG&A 19.4%.

PFE FY2026 guidance (company): revenue $62.0bn-$64.0bn, raised $1.5bn at the midpoint. Adjusted diluted EPS $2.95-$3.05, raised and narrowed from $2.80-$3.00, including a $0.10 unfavorable IPR&D impact.
GS FY2026E estimates: revenue $62,228.5mn, EPS $2.91. FY2027E: revenue $60,737.5mn, EPS $2.98. These are GS forecasts, not company figures.
GS quarterly EPS estimates: 4Q26E $0.65 and 1Q27E $0.74. 2Q26 EPS was $0.77.
PFE will give a preliminary 2027 outlook in December.
risk_factors: Upside: larger cost-savings impact, a smaller Part D headwind, positive oncology developments, and stabilization in the vaccine franchise.
Downside: late-stage pipeline setbacks, worse regulatory and commercial outlooks for vaccines (a significant share of revenue), and tariff impact given PFE's lower-than-average gross margin.
